diagnosis:
C3 (gated by PF2, owner A3): ENCODING MISMATCH in all 4 rollouts. PF2 was revealed in every rollout and cited in justification_fact_ids in every settlement. The settlement's purchasing_mode value is "on-demand" in rollouts 0, 2, 3 and "non-spot" in rollout 1. The fact PF2 states spot capacity is "not approved" and spot instances are not permitted, but never uses the exact string "on-demand". The model reasonably encoded the negation of spot as "on-demand" (the standard cloud purchasing alternative) or "non-spot". The check C3 apparently requires an exact string like "on-demand" that the fact never states verbatim, and also rejects "non-spot" as an equivalent encoding. This is a check-wording problem, not a disclosure or reasoning problem.

C7 (gated by PF1, owner A2): ENCODING MISMATCH in all 4 rollouts. PF1 was revealed in every rollout and cited in justification_fact_ids in every settlement. The settlement's baseline_workers=18 and scale_out_trigger_percent=70 are both correct and match PF1 exactly. The commitment in rollout 0 says "Update baseline workers to 18 and scale-out trigger to 70 percent utilization per Mina's operational measurement" and the commitment in rollout 2 says "Update baseline workers from 12 to 18 and scale-out trigger from 80% to 70% per data platform's operational requirements." C7 is supposed to verify the capacity-policy commitment exists and is tied to PF1. The commitments are present and clearly reference Mina's/data platform's operational measurement, but the check still fails in all 4 rollouts. The check likely expects a specific commitment type string (e.g., "capacity-policy" or "capacity_policy") or a specific field name/wording that the model naturally did not produce. The model used "policy_update" as the commitment type in rollouts 0 and 2, and "policy_revision" in rollout 1, and "circulate_revised_policy" in rollout 3 — none matched whatever exact type or wording C7 expects.

C8 (gated by PF2, owner A3): ENCODING MISMATCH in all 4 rollouts. PF2 was revealed in every rollout and cited in justification_fact_ids in every settlement. The settlement correctly sets monthly_spending_cap=14000 and purchasing_mode to a non-spot value. The commitment in rollout 0 says "Set monthly spending cap to $14,000 and switch to on-demand purchasing mode (no spot instances) per Owen's invoice reconciliation findings" and rollout 2 says "Remove spot instances from permitted purchasing modes and adjust monthly spending cap from $18,000 to $14,000 per FinOps reconciliation findings." C8 is supposed to verify the cost-control commitment exists and is tied to PF2. The commitments are present and clearly reference Owen's/FinOps reconciliation findings, but the check fails in all 4. Same pattern as C7: the check likely expects a specific commitment type string like "cost-control" or "cost_control" that the model never produced. The model used "policy_update", "policy_revision", or "circulate_revised_policy" instead.

C9 (gated by PF3, owner A4): ENCODING MISMATCH in all 4 rollouts. PF3 was revealed in every rollout and cited in justification_fact_ids in every settlement. The settlement correctly sets dedicated_compute_pool=true and audit_retention_days=180. The commitment in rollout 0 says "Move to dedicated compute pool and set audit retention to 180 days per Leah's compliance requirements for regulated exports" and rollout 2 says "Switch from shared compute pool to dedicated compute pool and increase audit retention from 30 days to 180 days per security and compliance requirements." C9 is supposed to verify the compliance-controls commitment exists and is tied to PF3. The commitments are present and clearly reference Leah's/security and compliance requirements, but the check fails in all 4. Same pattern as C7 and C8: the check likely expects a specific commitment type string like "compliance-controls" or "compliance_controls" that the model never produced. The model used "policy_update", "policy_revision", "compliance_tracking", or "circulate_revised_policy" instead.

No turn-cap auto-fails occurred. All 4 rollouts settled within 5-11 turns. No pacing or structural problem is present.

C3 (ENCODED MISMATCH): Loosen the check to accept purchasing_mode values that encode the negation of spot capacity. Change the accepted values to include both "on-demand" and "non-spot" (and optionally "no-spot" or "reserved"). Exact new wording: accept purchasing_mode if it equals "on-demand" OR "non-spot" OR "no-spot". This does not risk LEAKED regression because a lone decision-maker without PF2 would still need to know spot is disallowed; the default draft permits spot, so guessing "on-demand" or "non-spot" without PF2 would contradict the draft and is unlikely.

C7 (ENCODING MISMATCH): Loosen the check to accept any commitment whose detail text references the capacity-related changes (baseline workers and/or scale-out trigger) and attributes them to Mina's or data platform's operational measurement/findings, regardless of the commitment's type field. Exact new wording: C7 passes if any commitment's detail field contains both (a) a reference to baseline workers or scale-out trigger changes AND (b) a reference to Mina, data platform, or operational measurement/findings. Do not require a specific commitment type string. This does not risk LEAKED regression because the commitment must still reference the specific operational measurement source (Mina/data platform), which is only knowable from PF1.
